behavior.distinction_from_packet_49: Packet #49 (0x556e980, bsr clamp ladder) derives its bucket from a bit-scan-reverse ladder with min/max clamping semantics and an explicit default for the zero input. This window uses different mechanics: an unsigned divide first, then five independent shift tests, then an arithmetic cap (5 + (q >> 6 != 0)) with no bit-scan instruction anywhere and no clamp ladder. Same bucket purpose, different mechanism: div + shifts vs bsr. No shared primitive is claimed, and no census of bucketing windows was built.

The cs nopw/nopl/xchg groups are alignment padding inside the body between return blocks.
behavior.return_rule: eax = 0 when the unsigned quotient q = rdi / rsi is below 2, else min(floor(log2(q)), 6). Each ladder step re-tests the original quotient, and the cap is computed arithmetically as 5 + (q >> 6 != 0), so every q >= 64 maps to 6. A zero divisor is excluded: the hardware div traps, so no return value exists for that input.
